intervals.label: primary data-taking
intervals.note: December 2007 is the end of the dataset analysed in the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (168 extractions), not a stop of data-taking: that paper says measurements 'have continued'. The end is left open (ongoing as of 2026-10-25); the later status (Wikipedia: data to August 2011, ongoing in 2016-2017) was not confirmed by an authoritative source.
intervals.quote: Measurements have continued with only a few brief interruptions since that time. ... For all SAGE data from January 1990 through December 2007 (168 runs and 310 separate counting sets)

placements.note: Placed at site:baksan-sage-underground-lab. Start is the first month of SAGE data-taking (SAGE Collaboration 2009 paper, arXiv:0901.2200); the 1999 SAGE paper (arXiv:astro-ph/9907113) says extractions on about 30 tons of Ga at the Baksan laboratory began in 1988, so the gallium target was in place earlier than the start recorded here.
placements.quote: For all SAGE data from January 1990 through December 2007 (168 runs and 310 separate counting sets)

target_mass.note: 50 t is the mass stated in the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200). The target mass varied over time: the 1999 SAGE paper (arXiv:astro-ph/9907113) says the extraction mass was increased to nearly 60 tons in summer 1991, and Wikipedia gives a range of 50-57 tonnes.
target_mass.quote: The mass of gallium used in SAGE at the present time is 50 tonnes.

summary.plain: Tonnes of liquid gallium metal, deep in a Russian mountain, that solar neutrinos occasionally turn into germanium, which scientists then extract and count.
summary.technical: Radiochemical liquid-gallium-metal detector (50 t), 71Ga(νe,e⁻)71Ge reaction, at Baksan; chemically extracted and counted in periodic campaigns rather than observed in real time.

technology.note: Sourced from the SAGE Collaboration's 2009 paper (arXiv:0901.2200). The technology classes have no radiochemical value, so the class is 'other', as for detector:gallex-gno.
technology.quote: so the gallium metal remains molten. ... After a typical exposure interval of one month, the Ge carrier and 71Ge atoms produced by solar neutrinos and background sources are chemically extracted from the Ga.
technology.value: Radiochemical gallium detector: solar neutrinos capture on 71Ga to produce 71Ge via inverse beta decay in liquid gallium metal, which is chemically extracted and counted in periodic campaigns
